correctness.rationale: Monomial orthogonality gives norms (1+a^(n-N))/(1+a^-N) and correct unnormalized kernel. Positive coefficients c_n=(1+a^(n-N))^-1 have successive ratios c_{n-1}/c_n strictly increasing with minimum R_N=(a^N+a)/(a^N+1)>a. Enestrom-Kakeya on each finite Taylor polynomial excludes |s|<R_N; local uniform limit and Hurwitz transfer zero exclusion. In annulus a<|s|<1, H_N=s^-N F_N=sum_{j>=-N}s^j/(1+a^j) converges normally with derivatives to bilateral G_a. The classical Ramanujan 1psi1 product has numerator/denominator factors zero-free in that annulus, and net winding zero around a<|s|=r<1: each 1+c*s factor has zeros outside; each 1+c/s factor has one zero and one pole inside. Argument principle on F_N=s^N H_N then gives exactly N zeros inside each fixed circle. A second inner circle arbitrarily close to a and zero exclusion below R_N give radial collapse. For k>=1, sum of kth powers of N zeros equals contour integral s^k H_N'/H_N, which is uniformly O(1); divide by N and use radii -> a>0, plus conjugate negative moments, to prove Haar angular limit. Finite winding numerics are supporting only.
